problem: Prior relation-graph methods for object-goal navigation (e.g. ORG) build one rough graph over object categories, ignoring the agent-target relationship and the distinct roles of horizontal, vertical and depth relations. Transformer-based VTNet uses no explicit object relations.
motivation: Humans find a target by using the left-right layout of other objects when the target is not visible, and then use distance cues when approaching it. The paper argues that separate graphs for horizontal and distance relations, with the depth given only to the target, should give the agent a more useful visual representation.
key_idea: Build an Agent-Centric Relation Graph from two graphs: OHRG encodes horizontal box coordinates among objects, and ATDRG encodes vertical coordinates plus the estimated depth of only the target. The resulting graph feature is then fused with global image features by a transformer and fed to an A3C policy.
insight: Relations in different directions should be modelled in separate graphs, but not too many. One graph for all three relations (h./d./v.) gives SR 70.4 and three separate graphs (h.+d.+v.) gives 72.8, while ACRG (h. + d./v.) gives 77.6. Giving depth only to the target beats giving depth to all nodes (Multi-depth 68.8), and a graph for distance beats a plain depth vector (Simple-depth 71.4). Pre-training the transformer is essential: without it SR collapses to 10.2, while the transformer itself only adds about 2.5 SR (75.1 without vs 77.6).
method: Detection and depth: DETR gives 100 detections (box, confidence, label, 256-d feature); a pre-trained SARPN depth estimator gives a depth map, and object depth is the mean depth inside the box.
OHRG: a GCN with a learnable adjacency matrix (N=100) over nodes made of horizontal coordinates [h1,h2], confidence and label; Zh = ReLU(Ah Xh Wh).
ATDRG: a GCN over nodes made of vertical coordinates [v1,v2], confidence, label and depth; only the target node has a real depth and all other nodes are set to 0.
Fusion: Zh and Zd are concatenated and passed through an FC layer to give Zt, which is used as an attention map on the DETR appearance features (F = Zt·f).
Transformer: 1 layer with 8 heads; the graph feature F is the key/value and the ResNet18 position-encoded global feature is the query, giving the visual representation F̂.
Policy learner: F̂ is concatenated with a previous-action embedding, passed through an LSTM, and trained with A3C (16 workers, 2M episodes; reward +5 on success, -0.01 per step).

Pre-training: SARPN is trained on ground-truth depth to make pseudo depth for AI2-THOR; the transformer is pre-trained by imitating Dijkstra shortest-path expert actions, and DETR is fine-tuned on AI2-THOR.

setting.backbone: DETR (fine-tuned) + SARPN depth estimator (pre-trained) + ResNet18 + GCN graphs + 1-layer transformer + LSTM/A3C policy (trained with RL)
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR: 80 of 120 rooms for training, 22 target categories, 2M episodes; expert Dijkstra actions for transformer pre-training; ground-truth depth for SARPN pre-training; RoboTHOR: 500k episodes
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB only (depth is estimated by SARPN)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth depth and expert actions are used only in pre-training)

numbers.eval_set_note: 40 held-out test rooms (80 train / 40 test), all episodes
numbers.backbone: DETR + SARPN + transformer + LSTM/A3C, with the TPN module
numbers.extra: uses the TPN (Tentative Policy Network) module from ORG
numbers.evidence: Table I, ALL column: ACRG+TPN (Ours) 78.2(0.9) 0.457(0.007); Lopt>=5: SR 70.4, SPL 0.447

numbers_note: Numbers are on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR, which are not in the canonical benchmark list. The splits are the paper's own train/test room split, so 'test' is the closest label. SR is a percentage and SPL is printed as a fraction.
results: On AI2-THOR, ACRG reaches SR 77.6 (78.2 with TPN), beating VTNet's 72.2 (73.5 with TPN) and ORG's 65.3. Its SPL of 0.439 is on par with VTNet's 0.449, and it does better on long paths (Lopt>=10: SR 55.8 vs VTNet's 44.21). On RoboTHOR it reaches SR 12.5 vs VTNet 10.4 and ORG 9.97.
limitations: It fails when large objects fill the view (the agent cannot tell an object surface from floor) and when mirrors show reflected free space.

It needs multi-stage pre-training (depth estimator, transformer, fine-tuned DETR) because the transformer does not converge without it, and it is evaluated only in AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR simulation with absolute SR still low on RoboTHOR (12.5).
Graph combinations were not searched exhaustively, and SPL is not better than VTNet on the overall AI2-THOR set.
